extracted.intended_audience: journal publishers, editors, scientific societies, and researchers interested in peer-review equity
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes evidence of gender imbalance among peer reviewers and gives recommendations and measurable practices for publishers, editors, and societies to audit, monitor, and increase women’s participation as manuscript reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers should take additional steps to increase women reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: “Publishers of scholarly journals should take additional steps to get more women to serve as peer reviewers of manuscripts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly urges publishers to act (e.g., encourage invitations of women, especially younger women) and to lead inclusivity efforts across journals and societies; this is a high‑level requirement calling for concrete policy and outreach changes at publishing organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report the proportion of female peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The study found women accounted for 20 percent of all peer reviewers (2012–2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should track and publish reviewer gender proportions so they can be compared to relevant baselines (authors, membership) and monitored over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare reviewer gender proportions to baseline populations (authors and members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer share (20%) was lower than percentage of women accepted as first authors (27%) and lower than percentage of AGU members who are women (28%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use author and membership demographics as expected baselines when evaluating whether reviewer representation is equitable; report observed vs expected differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit reviewer and author demographics using transaction and membership data
rubrics_metrics.description: The study used information from AGU’s 20 journals and its member database, merging author and reviewer transactions (2012–2015) with members and AGU accounts (2013–2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When auditing, merge submission/reviewer transaction records with membership databases across multiple years to get a comprehensive dataset for analysis; document data sources and timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for age when analyzing gender bias
rubrics_metrics.description: “Accounting for age is necessary to explore bias because the proportion of women geoscientists decreases greatly with age.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify analyses by age groups (or otherwise control for career-stage/age) because aggregate gender proportions vary with age and can mask or distort biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor invitation and suggestion patterns by gender
rubrics_metrics.description: The lower number of female peer reviewers is a result of fewer women being suggested or asked to review journal articles by authors and editors, especially men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track who is being suggested and who is being invited (including author-suggested reviewers vs editor-invited) disaggregated by gender to identify where disparities in invitations arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track reviewer acceptance/decline rates by gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Slightly more women across all age groups also declined to be a peer reviewer when asked, according to the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report invitation acceptance and decline rates by gender to distinguish between disparities caused by invitation practices versus willingness/ability to accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage authors and editors to invite more women, especially younger women
rubrics_metrics.description: “Publishers should encourage authors and editors to invite more women to review manuscripts, especially younger women.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize this by setting encouragement policies, guidance documents for editors, or proactive reviewer-selection practices (e.g., reviewer suggestion tools, reminder prompts) that prioritize gender balance and early‑career women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train and educate editorial staff to combat implicit bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The results ... highlight the need for journal publishers to make additional efforts to train and educate their staff in combating gender bias in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide implicit-bias training, develop editorial policies that reduce bias in reviewer selection, and include bias-awareness in editor onboarding and performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage similar audits across societies, funders, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors encourage other scientific societies, funding agencies and publishers to consider similar audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other organizations should perform equivalent demographic audits of their reviewer and author records to determine whether similar patterns exist in their communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider other underrepresented groups in audits and interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors suggest considering how other underrepresented groups might be affected in similar ways to women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design audits and interventions to include race/ethnicity, disability, geographic location, and other axes of underrepresentation where feasible; recognize measurement challenges and document limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect demographic data beyond binary gender where possible, noting measurement limits
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is relatively easy for us to gather this binary gender data, but other underrepresented groups are not so easily measurable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand demographic data collection beyond a binary gender field where appropriate and feasible, but be transparent about what can and cannot be measured and ensure privacy and ethical data use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use acceptance rates by author gender as an outcome metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers with women first authors were accepted at a higher rate than papers with male first authors across all age groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include manuscript acceptance rates by author gender as an outcome to understand whether reviewer selection or other processes affect editorial decisions; interpret results alongside reviewer-demographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize peer review as a career-building activity and aim for equitable opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is described as an essential part of scholarly publishing and building a scientific career; reviewing helps scientists develop writing, expertise, and professional relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing policies, explicitly treat reviewer assignments as career-enriching opportunities and aim to distribute them equitably as part of retention and advancement strategies for underrepresented groups.
